task: Draft a clear dispute message to my bank's fraud team listing the payments I didn't make and asking how the ride-app charges will be handled.
text:
Hi, I need help writing to my bank's fraud team. On 3 October I noticed four card payments I never made: 89.99 euros to an online electronics shop, then three charges of 24.50 euros each to a ride app I don't even have installed. The statement shows the full card number, 4000 1234 5678 9010, and I've already blocked that card in the app. My husband, Nguyen Van Duc, has his own card on the same account and his payments look normal. The branch adviser, Mrs Oyelaran, told me on the phone that disputes must be filed within 13 months, but she wasn't sure whether the ride-app charges count as one dispute or three. Replies can go to lan.nguyen@example.com or 07700 900418.

Thanks,
Nguyen Thi Lan

text: My accountant, Hemi Walker, is on holiday until the 20th, so I'm trying to understand this tax letter myself. It's addressed to me, Aleksandra Wiśniewska, tax ID 7710-4482-93X, and says I underreported rental income for 2024 by 2,350 euros. task: Help me fix the loan formulas in my budget sheet and add a total-interest column.
text: Quick question about a budgeting spreadsheet. I'm loosely following the 50/30/20 rule that Elizabeth Warren and Amelia Warren Tyagi popularised in All Your Worth, and I'm adding a loan tab in Google Sheets. My formula is =PMT(0.06/12, 60, -10000) for a hypothetical 10,000 loan at 6% over five years, and it returns 193.33, which matches the loan calculator on the MoneyHelper website. But when the term cell contains text like "5 years" I get #VALUE!, and when I test a 0% rate in my homemade version, =P*r/(1-(1+r)^-n), it shows #DIV/0!. Is there a clean way to make the formula handle a zero rate, and should I use an IF with a simple division for that case? I'd also like a column showing total interest paid over the term. Please explain it as if I'm comfortable with spreadsheets but not with finance jargon.

  auth_token: tok-demo-7Qm2Vx9LrT
